gap: No result ChatGPT got states how fast three simultaneous streams fill the card: at DashCamTalk's measured bitrates the Vantrue N4 Pro S writes about 25 GB an hour (about 10 hours on a 256 GB card before loop recording overwrites) and the N4S about 20 GB an hour (about 13 hours), and none quotes Vantrue's manual that parking modes stop when power is cut, or the $24.99-$34.99 kit prices.
standout_why: Compared against Product Bible's best-3-channel page (cited) and Vortex Radar's best-dashcams page (cited, read through a text proxy because the direct fetch returned 403). Product Bible says only 'At least 256GB for daily driving, since three cameras fill a card faster than one or two' and that Vantrue takes cards up to 1TB; it gives no bitrate, no GB per hour, no hours per card, no hardwire kit price and no cutoff voltage. Vortex Radar gives general parking facts (traditional parking modes 'draw 300 to 600mA', most cams have 'a configurable voltage cutoff', A229 Plus 'Front cam quality drops w/ additional cameras', 512 GB card support) but no per-channel bitrate or card-hours for any 3-channel camera, and it mentions the N4 Pro S only in an image caption. ChatGPT's own answer already says parking mode needs a separately bought hardwire kit and a high-endurance card, so that part is not new; the hours-per-card arithmetic, the manuals' three-channel resolution tables, the kit prices and cutoff voltages are. The ezdashcam collection page (429) and the cited YouTube video were not read.
decides: It confirms the Vantrue pair rather than overturning it. Both manuals list their top resolution with all three cameras recording (N4 Pro S 4K/1080P/1440P, N4S 1944P+1440P+1440P, all 30 fps), so neither drops quality in 3-channel mode. The N4S writes about 20% less data per hour (at DashCamTalk's 1440p front setting) and leaves room under $300 for a parking kit: $199.99 + $29.99 = $229.98. The N4 Pro S at $279.99 goes over $300 with any Vantrue kit: $304.98 with the $24.99 kit, $309.98 with the $29.99 Voltage Display kit whose listing names it (all prices read 2026-11-21 except the N4 Pro S, read 2026-11-14 per the brief). So N4 Pro S is the pick if $300 covers the camera alone, N4S if parking mode has to fit inside the budget. The VIOFO A229 Pro 3CH writes at least 36.9 GB an hour from front and rear alone and tops out at a 512 GB card against Vantrue's 1 TB.

findings.note: Maker's PDF, text extracted through the r.jina.ai reader because the raw PDF would not parse. Order is front/cabin/rear. The manual has no 60 fps option and no note that HDR is unavailable in 3-channel mode. The front camera keeps 4K with all three channels on.

findings.label: Resolution options with front + cabin + rear recording together (maker's manual)
findings.value: Top setting 1944P front + 1440P cabin + 1440P rear, 30 fps; front-only maximum 2592x1944P 30FPS
findings.note: Maker's PDF, text extracted through the r.jina.ai reader. Other three-channel options: 1440P+1440P+1440P, 1440P+1080P+1440P, 1440P+1080P+1080P, 1080P+1080P+1080P, 1440P+720P+1080P, 1080P+720P+720P, all 30 fps. No resolution drop when the third camera is on.

findings.label: Average bitrate per channel (DashCamTalk)
findings.value: Front 32 Mbps (2160p 30 fps), rear 14 Mbps (1440p 30 fps), cabin 9.8 Mbps (1080p 30 fps); sum 55.8 Mbps
findings.source_title: Vantrue N4 Pro S (DashCamTalk review page)
findings.note: Page marked published December 21, 2025. Arithmetic: 55.8 Mbps / 8 x 3,600 s = 25,110 MB = about 25.1 GB per hour. Card holds 256 / 25.1 = about 10.2 h on 256 GB, 20.4 h on 512 GB, 39.8 h on 1 TB before loop recording overwrites. Decimal GB; audio, locked event files and formatting overhead ignored. The page also names the processor as Novatek NT98529.

findings.label: Bitrate per channel (DashCamTalk)
findings.value: 14.8 Mbps on each of the three cameras, listed at 2560 x 1440 30 fps; sum 44.4 Mbps
findings.note: Arithmetic: 44.4 Mbps / 8 x 3,600 s = 19,980 MB = about 20.0 GB per hour; 256 / 19.98 = about 12.8 h on 256 GB, 25.6 h on 512 GB, 50 h on 1 TB. DashCamTalk lists the front at 1440p, not the manual's 1944P top setting, so the 1944P front would write more per hour than this. The page does not call the figure an average.

findings.label: Average bitrate, front and rear (DashCamTalk)
findings.value: Front 57 Mbps (2160p 30 fps) + rear 25 Mbps (1440p 30 fps) = 82 Mbps before the cabin camera
findings.note: Page marked published December 22, 2023. Arithmetic: 82 / 8 x 3,600 = 36,900 MB = 36.9 GB per hour from two channels alone; 256 GB lasts at most about 6.9 h and 512 GB about 13.9 h, less once the 1080p cabin stream is added. Cabin bitrate is not given on the page.

findings.source_title: Vantrue N4 Pro S User Manual English (PDF)
findings.note: The manual has no recording-time table by card size and tells owners to format the card at least once a month. The N4S manual gives the same 32GB-1TB range, U3 or higher, and says to format every two weeks.

findings.label: Why parking mode needs a hardwire kit (maker's manual)
findings.value: Motion detection: "The device must remain continuously powered; it will automatically stop working if the power is cut off." Power: "Built-in super capacitor", input DC 5V 3A, 7 W
findings.source_title: Vantrue N4 Pro S User Manual English (PDF)
findings.note: The manual also says to use "the VANTRUE hardwire kit cable or other stable and continuous power supply" and that ACC mode "Requires proper wiring via an ACC hardwire kit cable". A supercapacitor stores no recording time, so with the power cut the camera records nothing. Working temperature -20°C to 60°C. The manual states no low-voltage figure; that is in the kit listings.

findings.label: Parking power requirement (maker's manual)
findings.value: "The device requires a stable power supply. If the power is disconnected, the dash cam will automatically shut down."; "We recommend using Vantrue ACC hardwire kit."
findings.note: Parking modes: collision detection, motion detection, low bitrate (1080P or 720P at 15 fps), low frame rate. Only one of time lapse and parking mode can be on. Built-in supercapacitor, DC 5V 2.4A, 7 W, working temperature -20°C to 60°C.

findings.label: Collision-detection parking mode start delay (DashCamTalk)
findings.value: DashCamTalk calls it "not useful as recording starts 10+ seconds after impact"; buffered motion detection, low bitrate and low frame rate modes are supported "with the purchase of an optional hardwiring kit"
findings.source_title: Vantrue N4 Pro S (DashCamTalk review page)
findings.note: Named-reviewer judgement. The Vantrue manual gives no latency figure: it says the camera "automatically powers on to record" a 30-second clip in power-saving mode.
